{{Short description|English mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Alfred William Goldie''' (10 December 1920, Coseley, [[Staffordshire]] – 8 October 2005, [[Barrow-in-Furness]], [[Cumbria]]) was an English [[mathematician]].

==Biography==
Goldie was educated at [[Wolverhampton Grammar School]] and then read [[mathematics]] at [[St John's College, Cambridge|St John's College]], [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge]].  His studies were interrupted by war work on [[ballistics]] with the Armament Research Department of the [[Ministry of Supply]], eventually taking his [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] in 1942 and [[Master of Arts|MA]] in 1946.

==Academic career==
Goldie became an assistant [[lecturer]] at the [[University of Nottingham]] in 1946.  In 1948 he was appointed lecturer in [[Pure Mathematics]] at what was then [[Colleges of Durham University|King's College, Durham]] (and has been the [[Newcastle University|University of Newcastle upon Tyne]] since 1963) where he was promoted to [[senior lecturer]] in 1958 and [[Reader (academic rank)|reader]] in [[algebra]] in 1960.

In 1963 Goldie was appointed [[Professor]] of [[Pure Mathematics]] at the [[University of Leeds]].  He retired from his chair in 1986 with the title [[emeritus]] [[professor]].<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.leeds.ac.uk/secretariat/obituaries/2005/goldie_alfred.html|title=Obituary: Alfred Goldie|publisher=[[University of Leeds]]|accessdate=11 September 2016}}</ref>

Goldie won the 1970 [[Senior Berwick Prize]] from the [[London Mathematical Society]], where he also served as vice-president from 1978 to 1980.

Goldie worked in [[ring theory]], where he introduced the notion of the [[uniform dimension]] of a module, and the [[uniform module|reduced rank]] of a module.  He is well known for [[Goldie's theorem]], which characterizes [[Goldie's theorem|right Goldie ring]]s.  Indeed, his ''[[The Independent|Independent]]'' obituary described him as the "Lord of the Rings".<ref name="independent">{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/alfred-w-goldie-6112848.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180323154741/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/alfred-w-goldie-6112848.html |archive-date=2018-03-23 |url-access=limited |url-status=live|title=Alfred W. Goldie: Algebraist 'Lord of the Rings'|work=[[The Independent]]|author=J. Chris Robson|date=1 January 2006|accessdate=11 September 2016}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Goldie married Mary Kenyon in 1944.  They had three children (from eldest to youngest): Isobel (Carlyle), Helen, and John. Both Isobel and Helen completed PhDs in Geography, while John completed a degree in music. Mary died in 1995 and in 2002 he married Margaret Turner, who survived him.<ref name="independent" />
